free_elimination.how: units digit: at x=11 every power ends in 1, so units = 1-3+3-1 = 0; only 1000 ends in 0

items.note: Expression is (x-1)^3 = 10^3 = 1000. Units-digit read kills all three distractors with no expansion.
Area factors (x+3)(x+4); sides 9 and 10 at x=6, perimeter 38. 90 is the area value; 40/42 are off-by-one sides. Parity (l+w odd -> perimeter 2 mod 4) would kill 40 but needs the factoring.

free_elimination.how: range bound: |x|<=7 and |y|<=4, so x-y<=11; 65 (49+16) and 33 (49-16) exceed it

items.note: x=7, y=-4 gives 11. After the bound only 3 and 11 remain and 'greatest' picks the larger, so the bound nearly is the item.

free_elimination.how: adjacency: stem asks for the least integer meeting an inequality (a ceiling); the set contains exactly one adjacent pair 33/34, so the key is one of those

items.note: 5n/12 >= 14 -> n >= 33.6 -> 34. 33 gives 13.75 (fails). Adjacency tell narrows to 33/34.

free_elimination.how: 48 is not a perfect square (area of a square); each rectangle has the square's side as one side and perimeter 30, so side < 15 and area < 225, killing 225 and 900

items.note: Rectangles s by s/4: 2(s + s/4) = 30 -> s = 12, area 144. Perfect-square property plus a bound off the printed perimeter kills all three.

free_elimination.how: triangle inequality: diagonal < length + width = half the perimeter = 28; kills 40, 28 and 192

items.note: 14k = 56, k=4, sides 16 and 12, diagonal 20. Half-perimeter bound kills every distractor.

free_elimination.how: limiting case: DOE = (AOB+BOC)/2 is independent of the 70; set AOB=90 and DOE=45+45=90

items.note: 35 + 55 = 90. Classic bisector-of-linear-pair fact; the 70 is a red herring, which a student who knows the fact reads off instantly.

free_elimination.how: folding in half reduces the outline: folded perimeter must be less than the original 2(12+8)=40, killing 40 and 48

items.note: Fold halves the 8 cm width: 12 by 4, perimeter 32. 28 is the wrong-fold (6 by 8) value; 32 vs 28 needs reading the fold direction.

free_elimination.how: bound: at most 4 toothpicks per square with sharing, so fewer than 4x25=100; kills 101 and 100

items.note: Next palindrome after 15951 is 16061; 16061 - 15951 = 110. 10 would give 15961 (not palindrome); 210 gives 16161, a later palindrome. No shortcut kills options.

free_elimination.how: magnitude: times are 62.47 s and 59.85 s, within ~3 s of each other; 42.62 and 57.38 are far too large
adjacency: place counted from the top is (number above her)+1, and the set holds exactly one adjacent pair 10/11

items.note: She beats 30 of 40, so 10 are above her: 11th. Adjacency tell narrows to 10/11; 30 is the count she beat.

free_elimination.how: bound: both probabilities lie in [0,1] and the theoretical one is 0.5, so the excess is at most 0.5; kills 3 and 0.56
magnitude: the median of a list running 2 to 100 must sit near the middle (~50); 25 and 2 are far from it

items.note: (50+52)/2 = 51. 52 is the 26th term; 51 is also the midpoint of the endpoints, so 51 vs 52 is the item.

free_elimination.how: denominator that cannot occur: the sample space is the 90 two-digit numbers, so the probability has a denominator dividing 90; 1/11 is impossible
divisibility: equal counts N is a multiple of 24, and packs = N/6 + N/8 = 7N/24, a multiple of 7; kills 16 and 32

items.note: N = 96: 16 + 12 = 28 packs. 21 (N=72) survives the multiple-of-7 cut; 'greatest' then picks 28.

free_elimination.how: multiple-of: n must be a multiple of 8; 90 is not

items.note: n multiple of lcm(8,30)=120; gcd(120,90)=30. 720 fails (gcd 90); 240 is valid but not least.
